label: first original token q being fed back at the first copy step (q at recall_idx 1)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and only when the input token is q. 94.5% of activation mass is at recall_idx 1, i.e. the step right after <DEL>, where the model gets its own echo of orig(0)=q back as input; every top example has the form q ... <DEL> [q]. Strength drops as sequences get longer: hit rate is highest for L 3-6, lower at L=7-8, and it is mostly silent at L=9 (the main false positives are L=9 at step 10). A weak secondary mode (about 23% of active steps but only 5.5% of mass, all in the bottom half of activations) fires on q at recall_idx 2, when orig(1)=q is fed back. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, on any other token, or on q at later copy positions (recall_idx >= 3).

issues: Core claims hold. The feature fires only in the copy phase and only on in_tok=q (100% of mass). The split is 94.5% of mass at recall_idx 1 and 5.5% at recall_idx 2. It never fires at recall_idx >= 3 (precision 0.0 on 57,749 q steps). Test scores reproduce: P 0.913, R 0.741, F1 0.818, mass recall 0.942.

There is a systematic miss that the explanation wrongly dismisses. The recall_idx 2 mode depends on length: it is silent at L=3-4 (P 0.00 and 0.05), fires at L=5 (P 0.65) and L=6 (P 0.57), and fades at L=7 (0.16) and L=8 (0.02). The agent only tried the unrestricted recall_idx==2 disjunct (P 0.24), which is why F1 dropped. Adding (recall_idx==2)&(L in 5..6) to the predicate raises test F1 from 0.818 to 0.880, recall from 0.74 to 0.94, and mass recall to 0.992. These missed steps are about 20% of active steps.

Small factual errors about length. Hit rate at recall_idx 1 is about 1.0 for L=3-7 (L=7 P 0.996), not 'lower at L 7-8'; it only drops at L=8 (P 0.58) and L=9 (P 0.14). Also, the predicate's false positives are all L=8 sequences at step 9, not 'mostly L=9 at step 10': L=9 is already excluded by the predicate.
The miss rendering confirms the secondary mode is weak (0.03-0.21 of max), but it is a clean, length-gated class, not scattered noise.
